questions.stem: Hydrated copper sulfate (blue) can be heated to form anhydrous copper sulfate (white) and water. Adding water to anhydrous copper sulfate turns it blue again. What type of reaction is this?

options.text: An irreversible decomposition reaction
A reversible reaction: the dehydration and hydration are forward and reverse reactions
Two separate unrelated reactions
A neutralisation reaction

questions.explanation: This is a classic reversible reaction: CuSO4.5H2O (blue) ⇌ CuSO4 (white) + 5H2O. The forward reaction (heating) is endothermic (energy must be supplied). The reverse reaction (adding water) is exothermic (the test tube gets hot). The same product can become the reactant for the reverse process.

questions.stem: If the forward reaction of a reversible process is exothermic with Delta H = -92 kJ/mol, what can you say about the reverse reaction?

options.text: The reverse reaction is also exothermic with Delta H = -92 kJ/mol
The reverse reaction is endothermic with Delta H = +92 kJ/mol
The reverse reaction has no energy change
The reverse reaction is endothermic with Delta H = +46 kJ/mol

questions.explanation: In a reversible reaction, if the forward reaction is exothermic, the reverse reaction is endothermic by the same magnitude. The energy released going forward must be absorbed going backward. So if the forward reaction has Delta H = -92 kJ/mol, the reverse has Delta H = +92 kJ/mol.

questions.stem: Ammonium chloride decomposes when heated: NH4Cl(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + HCl(g). White solid disappears from the bottom of a test tube and reforms as a white solid near the top. Why does it reform?

options.text: The gases condense because of high pressure
The cooler region near the top allows the reverse (exothermic) reaction to occur, reforming NH4Cl
The gases are pushed upward and solidify
The white solid sublimes and deposits without any chemical change

questions.explanation: The forward decomposition is endothermic (needs heat). As the NH3 and HCl gases rise to the cooler part of the test tube, they no longer have enough energy to remain as products. The reverse reaction (exothermic) is favoured at lower temperatures, so they recombine to form solid ammonium chloride. This demonstrates the reversibility of the reaction.

questions.stem: In an open container, a reversible reaction may not reach equilibrium. Why is a closed system required?

options.text: A closed system prevents contamination
In an open system, gaseous products can escape, preventing the reverse reaction from occurring
A closed system increases the pressure
Temperature can only be controlled in a closed system

questions.explanation: If gaseous products escape from an open container, they cannot participate in the reverse reaction. Without the reverse reaction occurring, equilibrium can never be established. A closed system keeps all reactants and products contained, allowing both forward and reverse reactions to proceed until rates are equal.

questions.stem: Anhydrous copper sulfate is used as a chemical test for water. When water is added, it turns blue and becomes warm. Which statement correctly describes the energy changes?

options.text: The hydration is endothermic because energy is needed to form bonds with water
The hydration is exothermic (releases heat), and the dehydration (reverse) is endothermic
Both the forward and reverse reactions are exothermic
The warmth comes from friction between the water and the powder

questions.explanation: The solution becomes warm when water is added, indicating that hydration (CuSO4 + 5H2O -> CuSO4.5H2O) is exothermic. For a reversible reaction, if one direction is exothermic, the other must be endothermic by the same amount. So dehydration (removing water by heating) is endothermic - it requires continuous heating.
